meta.title: Saturday Injera
meta.audience: PLACEHOLDER — replace with your real audience, e.g. 'my cousins in the diaspora, watching on their phones'
meta.intent: PLACEHOLDER — replace with your intent, e.g. 'they should feel that home is something you can still taste from far away'
meta.style_block: warm documentary photography, golden hour light, soft grain like 35mm film, earthy tones, gentle shadows

character_sheet.prompt: character reference sheet of Emaye, an Ethiopian grandmother in her sixties with a kind lined face, grey braided hair, wearing a white cotton netela with a woven green border; front view and three-quarter view, natural kitchen light
character_sheet.reference_notes: Every keyframe must show the same face, the same netela, the same kitchen. Check the face and hands before spending GPU time on a clip.

music.caption: gentle Ethiopian instrumental, solo krar plucks over a soft warm pad, pastoral and nostalgic, sparse texture with room for a voice, handmade feel

end_card.subtitle: written by our family, pictures and music generated with open models

shots.image_prompt: extreme wide shot of an old Ethiopian market street at golden hour, dusty light between low stone buildings, tiny figures carrying baskets
shots.motion_prompt: slow gentle push in, a few people walking through the far background, dust drifting in the light, camera steady

narration.text: Every Saturday of my childhood began the same way: before the sun, before the call to prayer, with the sound of my grandmother washing her hands.

shots.reason: Establishes where and when the story happens, and puts the narrator's relationship to Emaye in one line.
shots.music_cue: score enters soft, single krar notes

shots.image_prompt: medium shot of Emaye in her kitchen at dawn, kneading teff dough in a clay bowl, steam rising from a round mitad griddle beside her
shots.motion_prompt: her hands keep kneading the dough, slow breathing motion, steam drifts upward, camera locked off

narration.text: She mixed the teff the night before and let it sour, and she said the waiting was the whole secret.

shots.reason: First clear look at the main character doing the central ritual; the 'waiting' line plants the film's theme.
shots.music_cue: pad joins under the krar, very quiet

shots.image_prompt: close-up insert of weathered hands spreading pale teff batter in a slow spiral across a hot black mitad, tiny bubbles forming
shots.motion_prompt: the hand pours and spreads the batter in one slow spiral, bubbles rise and pop, steam, camera fixed

narration.text: The batter went on in one slow spiral, and the pan answered with a thousand small bubbles.

shots.reason: Texture insert: the most tactile image of the film; gives the audience the sound and feel of the ritual.
shots.music_cue: sparse, let the pan rhythm lead

shots.image_prompt: close-up of Emaye's face lit by warm kitchen light, eyes following the griddle, faint smile, steam softening the background
shots.motion_prompt: she slowly turns her head toward the camera and smiles slightly, camera pushes in gently

narration.text: She never measured anything. She said the batter tells you when it is ready, if you are patient enough to listen.

shots.reason: Emotional centre of the film: her face while she says the film's proverb-like line.

shots.image_prompt: medium shot from inside a dim kitchen, a child of about eight silhouetted in the bright doorway watching Emaye work, morning light in dust
shots.motion_prompt: the child shifts weight and takes one small step inside, Emaye stays working, light flickers gently, camera static

narration.text: I was that child in the doorway. Too young to help, too curious to leave, learning without knowing I was learning.

shots.reason: Introduces the narrator as a character and makes the memory personal rather than documentary.

shots.image_prompt: close-up of Emaye's hands tearing the first piece of warm injera from the mitad and offering it toward the camera, steam curling off the bread
shots.motion_prompt: the hands tear the piece and extend it slowly toward the camera, steam drifts, camera very slightly pushes in

narration.text: The first piece was never hers. It went to the child in the doorway, still too hot to hold.

shots.reason: The giving gesture is the heart of the story: generosity before comfort.
shots.music_cue: silence for one beat, then soft krar

shots.image_prompt: wide shot of a family gathered around a low mesob table sharing injera from the same platter, hands crossing the frame, warm lamplight at dusk
shots.motion_prompt: hands reach and take pieces of food, gentle laughter movement in shoulders, camera slowly pulls back

narration.text: By evening the whole street had found a reason to pass through her kitchen, because in her house there was always one more plate than there were guests.

shots.reason: Widens the story from grandmother and child to community; the payoff of her habit.
shots.music_cue: fullest point of the score, still gentle

shots.image_prompt: medium close shot of the empty kitchen at dusk, the mitad cooling on its stand, Emaye's stool beside it, blue evening light through the small window
shots.motion_prompt: dust settles in the last light, a curtain moves faintly, very slow push in, everything else still

narration.text: She is gone now, but every time I wait for anything, bread or news or grief, I hear her: the waiting is the whole secret. This film was made with AI so that her kitchen would not be forgotten.

shots.reason: Closure: connects the proverb to the present, states the film's purpose, and justifies the AI end card.
shots.music_cue: score resolves to the opening krar phrase, fade
